summary:
COSMIC TIME MACHINE is an interactive astronomical exploration platform that transforms scientific space data into an immersive learning experience. It combines NASA/SPHEREx archival observations, astronomical catalogues and NASA JPL Horizons ephemeris data to help users explore celestial objects and understand how the universe is observed across different wavelengths and time.

The platform features an interactive Deep Sky Viewer, an immersive object exploration experience, detailed astronomical information and a time-dependent Solar System visualisation. Its multi-wavelength explorer uses six genuine SPHEREx FITS cutouts across four infrared detector bands and three observation epochs, allowing users to compare supported observations of the Orion Nebula region.

By bringing astronomical observations, spectral information and planetary data together in one accessible interface, COSMIC TIME MACHINE makes complex space science easier to explore and understand. It aims to inspire curiosity about the universe while maintaining scientific accuracy and transparent data provenance.
details:
COSMIC TIME MACHINE is an interactive astronomical exploration platform designed to make the universe easier to explore, visualise and understand. It combines scientific observations, astronomical catalogues, infrared imaging and time-dependent planetary data into one immersive web-based experience.

The platform features an interactive Deep Sky Viewer where users can navigate celestial objects, search and select astronomical targets, and access their scientific information. Its Immersive Viewer provides object-specific artistic representations, while the Object Information Inspector presents available spectra, astronomical properties, scientific explanations and database details.

A distinctive feature is its Multi-Wavelength Explorer, which uses six genuine NASA/SPHEREx FITS image cutouts of the Orion (M42) region across four infrared detector bands and three observation epochs. Users can compare supported same-epoch observations to explore how astronomical image structures vary across wavelengths. The platform also integrates NASA JPL Horizons to visualise time-dependent Solar System positions through a Sun-centred orbital diagram.

The project was developed using Next.js, React, TypeScript and CSS, with astronomical data processing involving FITS image reading, World Coordinate System (WCS) transformations, TAN/SIP reprojection, image stretching and quality-flag handling. Its data architecture integrates NASA/SPHEREx archival products from the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive, supplementary 2MASS/WISE catalogue photometry and the JPL Horizons API. It is a software-based platform and does not require custom hardware.

Its creativity lies in combining astronomical exploration, infrared observation comparison, immersive visualisation and planetary time-based information within a unified interface. Rather than simply displaying space photographs, it connects celestial objects with their available scientific data and observational context.

The project aims to benefit students, educators, astronomy enthusiasts and the general public by making complex astronomical information more accessible and interactive. Its intended impact is to encourage scientific curiosity, improve understanding of multi-wavelength astronomy and demonstrate how publicly available space-science datasets can be transformed into meaningful educational experiences.

Throughout development, our team prioritised scientific accuracy, reliable data sources, astronomical coordinate alignment, observation quality, data provenance, visual clarity, accessibility and preservation of the distinction between genuine scientific measurements and generated artistic representations.
